name: GET /api/analytics/overview - lead response-time and conversion analytics
description:
Returns the analytics rollup the Analytics Dashboard renders: the capture-to-response funnel, the conversion rates between its stages, the response-time distribution, and a per-source-channel breakdown plus a per-day series. A read, so it answers 200. THIS IS NOT GET /api/sla/status. That endpoint is OPERATIONAL - a live triage view answering 'which clocks need somebody right now', with an attention list of open at-risk and breached leads. This one is ANALYTICAL - it answers 'how are we performing and where', aggregated over a closed historical window, with no per-lead rows at all. The two deliberately compute different things and neither is derivable from the other. FUNNEL: captured counts every lead that arrived in the window; routed counts those that reached an owner (leads.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL); responded counts those a human answered (leads.first_response_at IS NOT NULL); breached counts leads.sla_breached. CONVERSION RATES are stage-to-stage, each expressed 0..1 rounded to four decimals: routed_rate is routed/captured, response_rate is responded/routed, and breach_rate is breached over leads whose clock has CLOSED. Every rate is NULL rather than 0 when its denominator is empty - reporting a rate of zero for a window with nothing in it is a number a manager would act on, and the dashboard renders null as an em dash instead. RESPONSE TIMES are seconds from lead ARRIVAL (leads.created_at), not from assignment, matching POST /api/leads/:id/first-response: the prospect has been waiting since they submitted, and measuring from assignment would let a lead sit unrouted for an hour and still report a fast response. average, median and p90 are reported together because an average alone hides the tail that actually loses deals; all three are null when nothing in the window has been responded to. FILTERS: from and to bound the window by lead arrival (ISO 8601; to must be after from; the range is capped at 366 days); source narrows to one capture channel; owner_user_id narrows to one representative's queue. All four are optional and combine; omitting from and to reports the last 30 days. Protected by the authenticate guard - the Authorization header is required on this GET. QA: depends on register (which creates the user passed as owner_user_id), login, and a captured lead so the window is non-empty. The malformed-owner_user_id branch is documented in errorCases but has no automated case: owner_user_id is a foreign key, and MUST-36 requires every FK value to come from a captured producer value rather than a literal, so a deliberately malformed id cannot be expressed here. The 400 path is exercised by the inverted-window and unknown-source cases instead, and validateUuidParam itself is covered where it is used on a path param. ATTAINMENT is the one block on this endpoint that is NOT counted locally: it says how many closed clocks MET their response target, and the target and the business calendar it is judged against belong to ProjexCloud sdk-sla, not to LeadFlow. The server makes exactly ONE gateway call per request for the whole window, carrying the same from/to/source/owner_user_id filters, so the dashboard never fans out into a read per lead. attainment.delivered is true when sdk-sla answered and attainment.source is then sdk_sla; when the gateway is unconfigured (PROJEXCLOUD_GATEWAY_URL unset, as in every test environment), unreachable, or answers without a closed count, the server falls back to counting attainment from its own projection, delivered is false and source is local_wallclock. Reporting DEGRADES, it never fails: a gateway outage must not turn the dashboard into a 500, so there is no error status for an unavailable gateway on this endpoint and QA cannot provoke one from the client side. attainment_rate is met/closed, 0..1 to four decimals, null when nothing closed. CLOCK PROVENANCE qualifies the breach figures rather than adding to them: by_clock_source splits the SAME population as breach_rate's denominator by the clock that produced each verdict, a null clock_source means a closed clock the SLA monitor has not observed yet (a gap in the record, not a third clock), and mixed is true when more than one ATTRIBUTED clock judged the window - which makes the breach rate a blend of a business-calendar measurement and a wall-clock one, and the dashboard renders that caveat. Because both blocks depend on the environment's gateway configuration rather than on request input, neither is asserted in expectedResponse: pinning delivered:false would document the test environment instead of the contract, and the same case would fail the moment a gateway is configured. The delivered path is proven instead by the sdk-sla attainment tests in server/tests/integration/analytics.test.ts, which stub the gateway client at the HTTP boundary. The INVALID_TOKEN case sends a LITERAL malformed bearer token rather than {{static:invalid-token}}: MUST-64 documents the placeholder form for this case but MUST-38 forbids {{static:}} in any header, and a literal satisfies both - jwt.verify rejects it exactly the same way, which is all the case needs. COVERS: 'Dashboard displays key metrics accurately' - the funnel, conversion, response-time and attainment figures this endpoint returns are the metrics the dashboard renders, and the provenance block is what keeps 'accurately' honest when two different clocks are in play; and 'Users can filter data by various parameters' - the from, to, source and owner_user_id filters, which the happy-path case exercises together and which narrow every block in the response including provenance.

THE CODE-MATCH FINDING ON THIS FILE IS A VERIFIED SCANNER FALSE POSITIVE, recorded so the next reader does not re-investigate it and does not 'fix' a correct definition to satisfy a scanner. The review agent cannot follow the mount: routes/index.ts does router.use('/analytics', analyticsRoutes) and analyticsRoutes does router.get('/overview'), so the literal path never appears in one file. Same root cause as the note on authz/evaluate-post.json and the six ai definitions. Verified against the running server on :3010 rather than argued - authenticated GET answers 200, the same call with no bearer answers 401, and from/to inverted answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the 'to' field. Exactly what this definition declares.

testCases.name: Read the analytics overview for a bounded window
Reject a window whose end is before its start
Reject a source outside the capture-channel vocabulary
Reject a bearer token that fails verification

errorCases.when: from or to is present but not a parseable ISO 8601 date, to is not after from, the range exceeds 366 days, source is present but not one of the fourteen capture channels, or owner_user_id is present but not a well-formed UUID
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a Bearer token
the bearer token fails verification or has expired
